The Supreme Court decided that in a state in which there was no remedy for a denial of the right to counsel, counsel must be offered peremptorily or the accused must be allowed to protract his trial.
All that need be said about this particular defense was peremptorily rejected by Judge Young in a prior case.

The court may grant such an injunction and order of restitution if it is satisfied that the defendant has not raised a fair issue of fact but only has made a perfunctory defense. This is particularly true where the objection is peremptorily raised.
